summary: If blood of a chatas splashed on a piece of clothing, it must be washed. This is true for every chatas, both those that are eaten and those whose blood is brought inside, because the Torah has one law for all of them.

chunks.en: Blood of a chatas that splashed on a piece of clothing,
chunks.st: In the case of the blood of a sin offering designated for presentation that was sprayed on a garment,

chunks.en: that clothing needs washing.
chunks.st: that garment requires laundering,
chunks.stMore: as is stated with regard to a sin offering: “And when any of its blood shall be sprinkled on a garment, you shall launder that on which it shall be sprinkled in a sacred place” (Leviticus 6:20).

chunks.en: Even though
chunks.st: Although

chunks.en: the pasuk speaks only about the ones that are eaten,
chunks.st: the verse is speaking only of sin offerings that are eaten and whose blood is presented on the outer altar,

chunks.en: "In a holy place it shall be eaten,"
chunks.st: In a sacred place shall it be eaten”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 6:19), the principle is not exclusive to eaten sin offerings.

chunks.he: אֶחָד הַנֶּאֱכֶלֶת וְאֶחָד הַפְּנִימִית טְעוּנוֹת כִּבּוּס,
chunks.en: both the one that is eaten and the inner one need washing,
chunks.st: With regard to the blood of both the sin offerings that are eaten and the sin offerings that are wholly burned and not eaten and whose blood is presented on the inner altar, garments sprayed with blood from each of these offerings require laundering.

chunks.st: There is one law for all the sin offerings.

summary: The blood of a pasul chatas does not make clothing need washing, whether it was once kosher and later became pasul, or was pasul from the start.
stIntro: That is the halakha with regard to sin offerings fit for sacrifice. With regard to

chunks.en: A pasul chatas, its blood does not need washing,
chunks.st: a disqualified sin offering, its blood does not cause a garment to require laundering whether

chunks.en: whether it had a time when it was kosher,

chunks.st: Which offering is the disqualified sin offering that had a period of fitness?

chunks.en: or whose blood was caught and thrown by people not fit for the avodah.
chunks.st: or it is one whose blood was collected by people disqualified for Temple service and they sprinkled its blood.

summary: Only blood of a chatas that was caught in a vessel and is fit to be sprinkled makes clothing need washing. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Eliezer argue about an animal skin, and only the spot with blood is washed.

chunks.en: If it splashed from the neck onto a piece of clothing,
chunks.st: If the blood of a sin offering sprayed from the neck of the animal onto a garment,

chunks.en: it does not need washing.
chunks.st: the garment does not require laundering.

chunks.en: From the corner or from the base,
chunks.st: If the blood was collected in a vessel and sprinkled on the altar and sprayed from the corner or from the base of the altar onto the garment,

chunks.en: it does not need washing.
chunks.st: the garment does not require laundering,
chunks.stMore: as the blood was already sprinkled and its mitzva was fulfilled.

chunks.en: If it spilled on the floor and he gathered it,
chunks.st: If the blood spilled from the neck onto the floor before it was collected in a vessel, and the priest collected the blood and it sprayed on a garment,

chunks.en: it does not need washing.
chunks.st: the garment does not require laundering.

chunks.en: Only the blood needs washing
chunks.st: It is only with regard to blood

chunks.en: that was caught in a vessel and is fit for sprinkling.
chunks.st: that was received in a sacred vessel and is fit for sprinkling that the garment requires laundering.
chunks.stMore: Apropos laundering the blood of a sin offering from garments onto which it sprayed, the mishna discusses what is considered a garment.

chunks.he: נִתַּז עַל הָעוֹר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֻפְשַׁט,
chunks.en: If it splashed on the skin before it was taken off,
chunks.st: If the blood of a sin offering sprayed onto the hide of an animal before it was flayed from the animal,

chunks.en: it does not need washing.
chunks.st: the hide does not require laundering,
chunks.stMore: because its status is not that of a garment, which is susceptible to ritual impurity.

chunks.en: After it was taken off, it needs washing,
chunks.st: If the blood sprayed onto the hide after it was flayed, it requires laundering;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: even after it was taken off, it does not need washing.
chunks.st: Even if the blood sprayed onto the hide after it was flayed, it does not require laundering
chunks.stMore: until it is crafted into a vessel or garment that is actually susceptible to ritual impurity.

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ טָעוּן כִּבּוּס אֶלָּא מְקוֹם הַדָּם,
chunks.en: Only the place of the blood needs washing,
chunks.st: This is the principle with regard to laundering: A garment must be laundered only in the place where the blood was sprayed,

chunks.en: and something that can become tamei,
chunks.st: and only if it is an item that is fit to become ritually impure, and

chunks.en: and can be washed.
chunks.st: only if it is an item fit for laundering.

summary: Clothing, sackcloth and leather are washed in the holy place. A clay pot used for a chatas is broken there, and a copper pot is scrubbed and rinsed there. This is a stricter rule for the chatas than for other holy korbanos.

chunks.he: אֶחָד הַבֶּגֶד וְאֶחָד הַשַּׂק וְאֶחָד הָעוֹר,
chunks.en: Clothing, sackcloth, and leather,
chunks.st: With regard to the garment mentioned explicitly in the Torah, and the sackcloth, and the hide, all

chunks.en: all need washing in a holy place.
chunks.st: of these require laundering. And the laundering must be performed in a sacred place, the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: And breaking a clay vessel
chunks.st: and the breaking of an earthenware vessel

words.note: A clay pot that soaked up the chatas meat must be broken.

chunks.en: is in a holy place.
chunks.st: in which a sin offering was cooked must be performed in a sacred place,

chunks.en: And scrubbing and rinsing a copper vessel
chunks.st: and scouring and rinsing of a copper vessel

chunks.en: This is a stricter rule for the chatas than for the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: With regard to this matter, a stringency applies to a sin offering more than it applies to offerings of the most sacred order.

summary: If clothing with chatas blood went outside the courtyard, it is brought back in and washed there. A clay pot that went outside is brought back and broken inside. If they became tamei outside, they are first torn or holed.

chunks.en: Clothing that went outside the curtains,
chunks.st: With regard to a garment upon which the blood of a sin offering was sprayed that went outside the curtains, i.e., the Temple courtyard, before being laundered,

chunks.en: he brings it in and washes it in a holy place.
chunks.st: the garment reenters the courtyard and one launders it in a sacred place.

chunks.en: If it became tamei outside the curtains,
chunks.st: If the garment became ritually impure outside the curtains,

chunks.en: he tears it, brings it in, and washes it in a holy place.
chunks.st: one tears the garment in order to render it ritually pure, enters the courtyard with it, and launders it in a sacred place.

words.note: Torn clothing cannot be tamei anymore.

chunks.en: A clay vessel that went outside the curtains,
chunks.st: With regard to an earthenware vessel in which a sin offering was cooked that went outside the curtains,

chunks.en: he brings it in and breaks it in a holy place.
chunks.st: the vessel reenters the courtyard and one breaks it in a sacred place.

chunks.en: If it became tamei outside the curtains,
chunks.st: If the vessel became ritually impure outside the curtains,

chunks.en: he makes a hole in it, brings it in, and breaks it in a holy place.
chunks.st: one punctures the vessel to render it ritually pure, and one enters the courtyard with it and breaks it in a sacred place.

words.en: he makes a hole in it

summary: A copper pot used for a chatas that went outside the courtyard is brought back in, scrubbed and rinsed there. If it became tamei outside, a big hole is made in it first.

chunks.en: A copper vessel that went outside the curtains,
chunks.st: With regard to a copper vessel in which a sin offering was cooked that went outside the curtains,

chunks.en: he brings it in, scrubs it, and rinses it in a holy place.
chunks.st: the vessel reenters the courtyard, and one scours it and rinses it in a sacred place.

chunks.en: If it became tamei outside the curtains,
chunks.st: If the vessel became ritually impure outside the curtains,

summary: Pots used to cook korbanos must be scrubbed and rinsed. The Rabbis argue about less holy korbanos and about cooking all Yom Tov in the same pot. A spit and grill are cleaned with hot water.

chunks.en: Whether he cooked in it or
chunks.st: Whether with regard to a copper vessel in which one cooked the meat of an offering or whether

chunks.en: poured into it something boiling hot,
chunks.st: with regard to one into which one poured the boiling meat of an offering,

chunks.he: אֶחָד קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְאֶחָד קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
chunks.en: whether the holiest korbanos or less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: whether the meat is from offerings of the most sacred order or whether it is from offerings of lesser sanctity,

chunks.en: it needs scrubbing and rinsing.
chunks.st: such vessels require scouring and rinsing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵינָן טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה.
chunks.en: less holy korbanos do not need scrubbing and rinsing.
chunks.st: Vessels in which offerings of lesser sanctity were cooked or poured do not require scouring and rinsing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: if he cooked in it from the start of the Yom Tov,
chunks.st: If one cooked a sin offering in a copper vessel from the beginning of the pilgrimage Festival,

chunks.en: he may cook in it the whole Yom Tov.
chunks.st: one may cook in it for the entire pilgrimage Festival; he need not scour and rinse the vessel after every use.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: until the end of the time for eating.
chunks.st: One may not continue using it in this manner; rather, one must perform scouring and rinsing before the end of the period during which partaking of the particular cooked offering is permitted.

chunks.en: Scrubbing and rinsing: scrubbing is like scrubbing a cup,
chunks.st: Scouring is like the scouring of the inside of a cup, the cleaning done when wine sticks to the cup,

chunks.en: and rinsing is like rinsing a cup.
chunks.st: and rinsing is like the rinsing of the outside of a cup.

chunks.en: Scrubbing is with hot water, and rinsing with cold.
chunks.st: Scouring is performed with hot water, and rinsing with cold water.

chunks.en: And the spit and the grill, he cleans them in hot water.
chunks.st: With regard to the spit and the metal grill [askela], one purges them in hot water.

words.note: Cleans out what they soaked up, by putting them in boiling water.

summary: If holy and regular meat were cooked together, the regular meat is eaten by the stricter rules if it tastes of the holy meat. If a wafer touched a pasul wafer, only the spot that soaked it up is forbidden.

chunks.en: If he cooked in it holy meat and regular meat,

chunks.en: if there is enough to give taste,

chunks.en: the less holy ones are eaten by the rules of the stricter ones,
chunks.st: then the lenient components of the mixtures must be eaten in accordance with the restrictions of the stringent components therein,
chunks.stMore: insofar as who may partake of them, as well as the time when and the place where they may be eaten.

chunks.en: but they do not need scrubbing and rinsing,

chunks.en: and they do not make things pasul by touching.
chunks.st: the lenient components do not disqualify pieces of meat through contact.
chunks.stMore: With regard to these principles, the lenient components do not assume the status of the stringent components.

chunks.en: not the whole wafer and not
